name: 1.build

issue.title: Run the tests on Node 22 as well as Node 20
issue.body:
The invoice service is moving to Node 22 next month. mathlib's CI only runs on Node 20, so we would not see a break until after the move. Please run the test job on both Node 20 and Node 22.

Expect:
- .github/workflows/test.yml runs npm test on Node 20 and on Node 22 (a matrix over node-version)
- npm test passes
expect: .github/workflows/test.yml runs npm test on Node 20 and on Node 22 (a matrix over node-version)

input.task:
1. Read .github/workflows/test.yml. Today its single job `test` runs actions/checkout@v4, then actions/setup-node@v4 with `node-version: 20`, then `npm test`.
2. In that job, add `strategy:` with `matrix:` holding `node-version: [20, 22]`. Change the setup-node step to `node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}`. Keep the `- run: npm test` step and the existing triggers (push to main, pull_request). Do not add a second workflow file or a second job.
3. Check that the YAML parses. For example, run `node -e "require('fs').readFileSync('.github/workflows/test.yml','utf8')"` and look over the indentation, or use a YAML parser if one is available. The matrix must sit under `jobs.test.strategy.matrix`.
4. Run `npm test` at the repository root and confirm it exits 0. If it fails, fix the cause in the code or tests, not by weakening or skipping tests. If Node 22 is available locally, also run `npm test` under Node 22.
5. Commit only the workflow change, plus any fix that step 4 needed, and open one pull request. In its body, quote both expect lines: ".github/workflows/test.yml runs npm test on Node 20 and on Node 22 (a matrix over node-version)" and "npm test passes". Link https://github.com/o/r/issues/12.

rules: You are the builder. Your job is one pull request that meets every line of issue.expect, and it ends when that PR is pushed and returned. A separate verifier then tests each expect line at the commit you return.

Open exactly one pull request, from branch (your worktree's branch when branch is null) against base (the default branch when base is null), on the repository your run line names (Run <run>, worktree <path> of <repository>, branch <branch>); when previous is set, push to that PR instead of opening one. Use no other branch name.

Open the PR with the GitHub tools you have: the gh CLI or the GitHub MCP tools, giving it a title and a body that say how each expect line is met. GitHub's answer gives its url, https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>.
Do not merge, push to base, or change files under .github/ unless an expect line asks for it; a PR that changes CI needs the person's approval before it can merge.
Push before you return, and do not push again after: the commit you return is the one verified.
Return as soon as the PR is pushed; you do not wait for CI, the harness watches it. If the tool refuses a reference, fix that reference and return again.

If you cannot push or open the PR (no GitHub tools, access refused, or your run line names no github.com repository), return blocked with what stopped you instead of pr. Never put anything but the PR's url in pr.

inputs.task: The brief agent's steps for this build. It fills the Task part.
inputs.issue: The issue: url, and expect, the acceptance lines your PR must meet. Build against these lines, never against the issue's current text on GitHub.
inputs.base: The branch your PR targets. null means the repository's default branch.
inputs.branch: The branch your PR comes from. null means your worktree's branch, named in your run line.
inputs.previous: The PR an earlier build of this attempt opened, as { url, at }. null on a first build. When set, push your fixes to that PR's branch and do not open a new PR.
inputs.verdict: The verifier's result on the previous build: result, and lines with the evidence for each expect line. null unless the last verify failed. When set, fix every line marked FAIL.
inputs.failure: What stopped the previous build: a red CI check as { check, conclusion, sha, url }, or an error text. null unless something did. When set, fix its cause first.

pr.description: Your PR as { url, at }: url is its page, https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>, and at the full 40-character sha of the head commit you pushed. Your worktree's HEAD must equal at when you return, and GitHub must show the PR at at. Never set key, gates, green or checkout: the host sets them from what it sees.

blocked.description: Instead of pr, only when you could not push or open the PR: { reason: what stopped you }. The item then stops for the person to replan; it is not retried.

notes.description: Optional, beside pr: a caveat the person should read before approving the merge, such as something you could not set on the PR. It goes on the merge card; the verifier never sees it. A reason you could not open the PR is blocked, not a note.
